summary:
Our project is a creative educational story inspired by NASA's challenge, Abandoned but Not Forgotten. We wanted to highlight the amazing machines humans have sent to the Moon and Mars, which remain there even after completing their missions.
Through our interactive story, we take young readers on an exciting journey into space, introducing them to forgotten robotic explorers and their important contributions to space exploration.
We created our story using ScratchJr, a beginner-friendly coding application that allows us to combine characters, backgrounds, movement, and storytelling. We used it to create animated scenes that make learning about space fun, visual, and interactive.
Our main goal is to help children understand that these machines are more than abandoned equipment. They are part of human history! Every rover, lander, and scientific instrument has its own story, mission, and contribution to science. Although their missions may end, their discoveries continue to inspire future generations.
We chose storytelling because we believe children learn best when information is presented in a fun, imaginative, and memorable way.
Through this project, we hope to:
Inspire children to explore space and learn about NASA missions.
Introduce young audiences to the equipment left on the Moon and Mars.
As the Al Nahda Young Innovators Team, we believe every space explorer deserves to be remembered.
Because even when the machines stop working, their stories never stop inspiring!
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten 🚀

Our project is a creative educational story inspired by NASA's challenge, Abandoned but Not Forgotten. We wanted to highlight the amazing machines humans have sent to the Moon and Mars, which remain there even after completing their missions.

Through our interactive story, we take young readers on an exciting journey into space, introducing them to forgotten robotic explorers and their important contributions to space exploration.

We created our story using ScratchJr, a beginner-friendly coding application that allows us to combine characters, backgrounds, movement, and storytelling. We used it to create animated scenes that make learning about space fun, visual, and interactive.

Our main goal is to help children understand that these machines are more than abandoned equipment. They are part of human history! Every rover, lander, and scientific instrument has its own story, mission, and contribution to science. Although their missions may end, their discoveries continue to inspire future generations.

We chose storytelling because we believe children learn best when information is presented in a fun, imaginative, and memorable way.

Through this project, we hope to:

  • Inspire children to explore space and learn about NASA missions.
  • Introduce young audiences to the equipment left on the Moon and Mars.
  • Explain how robotic explorers helped scientists discover more about other worlds.
  • Encourage creativity, curiosity, and interest in science, technology, engineering, and coding.

As the Al Nahda Young Innovators Team, we believe every space explorer deserves to be remembered. Their missions may have ended, but their discoveries will continue to shape the future of space exploration.

Because even when the machines stop working, their stories never stop inspiring!
